## redesign-door-d-marker-order-self-exclusion · contradiction · high · ticketed

**Fact:** Door (d) of the redesign runbook instructs a redesign-first cycle to set last_step to 'redesign: <id>' FIRST and then run redesign-pickup.js --next, asserting --next "takes that same ticket". It cannot. public.redesign_due_ticket() takes no cycle id, and its cooldown clause excludes any ticket named by a cycle started in the last 24 hours (c.last_step like 'redesign: ' || p.backlog_id || '%'), which matches the CALLING cycle's own marker. Proven live this cycle by a controlled toggle on the live function: the pre-boot gate named AGT-237 (refusal_parked_tickets() row 1, need_score 5, queue 113); after writing the marker 'redesign: AGT-237' the function returned AGT-251 (row 3, need_score 3, queue 244) and --next picked AGT-251; after clearing the marker the function returned AGT-237 again and --next picked AGT-237. The only marker in the trailing 24h was this cycle's own. Effect: every redesign-first cycle that follows the instruction literally skips the gate's named ticket and redesigns the next admitted one, so the highest-need blocked ticket is systematically passed over - defeating John's standing decision f8e2a234 (a blocked ticket stops the line) in the one place it is enforced. This cycle corrected the order by hand (cleared the marker, re-ran --next, took AGT-237, then wrote the marker after the pickup) and recorded both readings.

**Locations:**
- `undefined` — "undefined"
- `undefined` — "undefined"
- `undefined` — "undefined"

**Proposed resolution:** Either (1) give redesign_due_ticket() a p_cycle_id argument and exclude that cycle from the cooldown clause (c.id <> p_cycle_id), dropping the stale overload in the same migration per .claude/rules/supabase-function-signature.md, and have redesign-pickup.js pass --cycle-id on --next; or (2) change door (d) and the script header so the marker is written AFTER the pickup returns, naming the ticket actually handed - which is also what makes the marker a cooldown for the NEXT cycle rather than an exclusion for this one. (1) is preferred because it keeps the marker-first ordering that protects against a concurrent peer taking the same ticket while max_lanes > 1; (2) alone reopens that race. Either way the two selectors must agree, and a regression test should assert that the ticket the gate names is the ticket --next returns for a cycle whose own marker names it.

**Ruling:** docs/runbooks/redesign-after-refusal.md door (d) tells a redesign-first cycle to set last_step to 'redesign: <id>' first -- the runbook calls that line the cooldown marker -- and then run scripts/redesign-pickup.js --next, asserting that --next takes that same ticket. It cannot: public.redesign_due_ticket() takes no cycle id (nothing in redesign-pickup.js passes p_cycle_id, and the --next path posts rpc/redesign_due_ticket with no cycle argument), and its cooldown clause excludes a ticket a cycle has just marked. So the step written to guarantee the pickup is the step that prevents it, and the cycle silently redesigns a different ticket or none. / Either give redesign_due_ticket() a p_cycle_id argument and exclude that cycle from its own cooldown (c.id <> p_cycle_id), dropping the stale overload by its full identity argument list in the same migration per .claude/rules/supabase-function-signature.md, and pass --cycle-id on --next; or reverse door (d) so the marker is written after the pickup has named the ticket. Whichever way, grade the omitted-parameter path as well as the new one -- an overload break is invisible from the new call and total from the old -- and assert the picked id equals the marked id.
